findings.highlight: she's aiming for a private university
findings.evidenceJa: 美穂子、成績いいし、それに私立だから、少しくらいは融通利くと思うし
findings.explanation: Koharu says Mihoko has good grades and that their high school is private, so the school may have some administrative latitude about her attendance and graduation. The English instead says Mihoko is aiming for a private university, which provides no reason for the high school to accommodate her and misidentifies the relevant institution.
findings.japanese:
「あ、いえ、多分そんなことは…
美穂子、成績いいし、それに私立だから、
少しくらいは融通利くと思うし」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, no, I don't think that will be the case… Mihoko has good grades and she's aiming for a private university, after all, so I imagine there'll be room to accommodate her."

findings.highlight: he ran away all of a sudden, so I panicked and chased after him
findings.evidenceJa: あの人も意地張って逃げるもんだから、わたしも頭に来ちゃって、制服のまま店の外に出て、駅前追いかけてさぁ
findings.explanation: Koharu explains that Haruki stubbornly fled and that this made her angry enough to run after him in uniform. The English changes stubbornness into suddenness and her anger into panic, materially rewriting the confrontational, meddlesome impulse she is trying to explain to Mihoko.
findings.japanese:
「…うん。で、あの人も意地張って逃げるもんだから、
わたしも頭に来ちゃって、制服のまま店の外に出て、
駅前追いかけてさぁ」
findings.todokanai: "…Right. Well, he ran away all of a sudden, so I panicked and chased after him while still in my uniform, all the way to the front of the station."

findings.highlight: This is what it takes to be honest to absolutely everyone
findings.evidenceJa: そっかぁ…『誰に対しての誠実』って、こういうことか。ほんと、わたしもまだまだだね
findings.explanation: Koharu realizes that the question is 'honesty toward whom': full disclosure may be honest toward Mihoko but betray Haruki. The English turns this conflict between incompatible loyalties into the impossible ideal of being honest to everyone, losing the ethical distinction that leads her to choose silence.
findings.japanese:
「そっかぁ…『誰に対しての誠実』って、こういうことか。
ほんと、わたしもまだまだだね」
findings.todokanai: "I see… This is what it takes to be honest to absolutely everyone. I guess I still have a long way to go."

findings.highlight: if you keep that sour face up
findings.evidenceJa: これ以上杉浦が辛い顔してたら、俺が直接矢田さんと話そうとするかもしれない
findings.explanation: Haruki threatens to intervene if Koharu continues looking pained or distressed. 'Sour face' suggests irritation or bad temper, changing the suffering that motivates his offer and miscoloring her emotional state after the fight.
findings.japanese:
「だからさ…これ以上杉浦が辛い顔してたら、
俺が直接矢田さんと話そうとするかもしれない」
findings.todokanai: "That's why… if you keep that sour face up, Sugiura, I may have to go talk to Yada-san myself."

findings.highlight: I couldn't stand the thought of not having you by my side
findings.evidenceJa: それでも俺、あのときは杉浦が必要だった。君がいなくちゃダメだった
findings.explanation: Haruki says that at that time he needed Koharu and could not have managed without her. The English changes practical and emotional dependence during his collapse into an aversion to the thought of her absence beside him, a more possessive romantic declaration than the source supports.
findings.japanese:
「それでも俺、あのときは杉浦が必要だった。
君がいなくちゃダメだった」
findings.todokanai: "Even so, I needed you back then, Sugiura. I couldn't stand the thought of not having you by my side."

findings.highlight: the proof of her own nobility
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の情けなさが露見した瞬間には、自分が手に入れた優位を、嬉しそうに笑う。
findings.explanation: When Haruki's helplessness is exposed, Koharu happily smiles at the advantage or upper hand she has gained by being needed. The English calls this proof of her nobility, turning a teasingly unequal relational position into moral virtue and obscuring what makes her laugh.
findings.japanese:
それでも杉浦は、
俺の情けなさが露見した瞬間には、
自分が手に入れた優位を、嬉しそうに笑う。
findings.todokanai: The moment she saw the pathetic side of me, as well as the proof of her own nobility, Sugiura smiled happily.

findings.highlight: She hasn't forgiven me, and I haven't even attempted to gain her approval
findings.evidenceJa: 許してもらってないのに。認めてもらおうとしてすらいなかったのに。
findings.explanation: The immediate issue is Haruki's sudden use of 小春 at line 186: he has not received permission for first-name address and had not even tried to ask. The English turns 許す into forgiving a wrongdoing, obscuring the social boundary whose crossing prompts Koharu to answer with 春希先輩.
findings.japanese:
許してもらってないのに。
認めてもらおうとしてすらいなかったのに。
findings.todokanai: She hasn't forgiven me, and I haven't even attempted to gain her approval.

findings.highlight: if we want to overcome this together
findings.evidenceJa: だから、一緒に踏み越えれば…
findings.explanation: After they exchange first names, Haruki thinks that if they cross the boundary together, neither has to retreat alone from the breach in formality. The English makes this a generic wish to overcome their troubles together, deleting the linguistic and relational line they have just stepped across.
findings.japanese: だから、一緒に踏み越えれば…
findings.todokanai: That's why, if we want to overcome this together…
